title: Winters' Rescue
description: Master Sgt. Spring Winters, 403rd Maintenance Squadron training manager, talks about her connection to training Airmen and how it relates to her volunteer work doing K9 search and rescue.

transcript.text: (forlorn music)
- It's Master Sergeant Spring Winters,
I'm the Unit Training Master for the 403rd training group.
We track all the training whether it's
auxiliary training, testing formal schools,
basically keeping track of all the training program
for the entire maintenance group.
I love the interaction with people, and I love
maintenance, so that's the biggest part of it.
I started with the search and rescue team
back in about March of 2013.
We were searching for a couple of
missing kayakers in the local area.
I used my kayaking skills to help out
originally, and then I found that they
had a great canine team, so I started training canine.
We're a completely volunteer organiation
throughout the entire coast, so we've gone
to help as far as Louisiana and as far as Florida
on different searches.
Being a volunteer, there's chances of
you getting up in the middle of the night
and searching for total strangers
for those who you don't know,
who don't know you, and we're willing to
volunteer and give up our time with friends, family.
We train every weekend, I don't have a UTA.
And it's that service that we give back
to the community.
It's a sense of community, it's a sense
of giving back, bringing lost loved
ones back to their families.
It's a sense of commitment for our community
for as much as they do for us in the military.
Service before self goes beyond near forests
and in search and rescue, it's know that we are
ready to go at any given moment
when it's least expected, and we're ready
to perform and give a hundred percent.
As a training manager, when you're preparing
these guys, and getting them trained
and making sure that all their training
requirements are done, then you see
them leave to deploy, and you see them
come back from deployment knowing that
they completed their mission as a
fully trained technician.
You know, that's when it, that's when it counts,
when you see these young, new trainees
as they grow up to become supervisors
and you look back at them, and that's rewarding,
and we see that same thing with search and rescue.
